ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A transverse simple harmonic wave propagates along the $x$-axis. Figure A shows the waveform at time $t=0$, where $P$ is a particle in the medium located at $x=4\mathrm{m}$, and the position coordinate of particle $Q$ at $t=0$ is as shown in the figure. Figure B shows the vibration graph of particle $P$, and the shape of the vibration graph is similar to the waveform at time $t=0$.

1. What is the propagation direction and wave speed of this mechanical wave?
2. What are the horizontal coordinate \( x_{Q} \) of particle \( Q \) at time \( t=0 \) and the vibration equation of particle \( Q \)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Propagating in the positive direction of the $x$-axis at $1\mathrm{m/s}$.
$x_{Q}=8\frac{2}{3}\mathrm{m},y=2\cos(\frac{\pi}{4}t+\frac{\pi}{3})\mathrm{cm}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Figure A is the y-x waveform graph at t=0, the vertical axis unit is cm, and the horizontal axis unit is m; the wave crest is approximately at x=2 m and y=2 cm, and the wave trough is approximately at x=6 m and y=-2 cm, so the amplitude is 2 cm, and half a wavelength is 4 m. Point P is located at x=4 m, where the waveform passes through the equilibrium position and the spatial slope is negative. Point Q is on the rising branch to the right of x=8 m, and the dashed line marks its displacement y=1 cm. Figure B is the y-t vibration graph of point P, the vertical axis unit is cm, and the horizontal axis unit is s; the maximum displacement is approximately at t=2 s, the minimum displacement is approximately at t=6 s, and the amplitude is also 2 cm; at t=0, point P passes through the equilibrium position and moves in the positive y direction, and the time slope is positive. Reasoning: From Figure A, the distance from the wave crest to the adjacent wave trough is 4 m, therefore λ=8 m. From Figure B, the interval from maximum to minimum is 4 s, namely T/2=4 s, so T=8 s. The spatial slope ∂y/∂x<0 of point P at x=4 m, while from the vibration graph, the velocity ∂y/∂t>0 of point P at t=0. If the wave propagates in the +x direction, there is ∂y/∂t=-v∂y/∂x, and a negative spatial slope corresponds to a positive velocity, which agrees with the image; therefore the wave propagates along the positive direction of the x axis. The wave speed v=λ/T=8/8=1 m/s. For Q, the waveform at t=0 can be written as y(x,0)=2 sin(πx/4) cm. Q is located on the rising branch after x=8 m and y=1 cm, so 2 sin(πx_Q/4)=1, and taking the phase on this branch πx_Q/4=2π+π/6 gives x_Q=26/3 m=8 2/3 m. The angular frequency of Q is ω=2π/T=π/4 rad/s. Suppose the vibration of Q is y_Q=2 cos(ωt+φ) cm. From y_Q(0)=1 cm, get cosφ=1/2. Q has a positive spatial slope at t=0, and the wave propagates in the +x direction, so the initial velocity ∂y/∂t=-v∂y/∂x<0; while y'_Q(0)=-2ω sinφ<0, therefore sinφ>0, take φ=π/3. Therefore y_Q=2 cos(πt/4+π/3) cm.
